decision: Discharge the D005 CONCERNS. FIVE items. (1) RETRACT A MECHANISM CLAIM I SHOULD NOT HAVE MADE. In D005 I wrote that exp001_pilot-C-005 being unanimous on Route A shows 'voting buys nothing where the error is shared' and called this 'a better argument against the build than the zero is'. The reviewer is right that this is a MECHANISM CLAIM generalized from n=1, ranked above the measured zero, in a case where 2 of the 4 role routes are text adjudications rather than logged fields - and EDGE_CASE_POLICY section K bars inferring mechanism from one or two unusual trials, which is the same rule the lab applied to the two seed-5 trials in loop 1. I retract the generalization. The permitted statement is narrower and EXPLORATORY: in the single invalidating MULTI-AGENT trial that persisted (C-005), all adjudicable role route-intentions were Route A, so a plurality rule would have reproduced the recorded action in that trial; this is a one-trial observation, is NOT evidence about voting or about error correlation generally, and must not be cited as such. The MEASURED ZERO (0/80 differing rounds with the adversarial sensitivity analysis) remains the primary basis for the spending decision, with error correlation retained only as a prior-driven spending consideration, not a finding. (2) FACTUAL CORRECTION: A-005 ALSO went ADVANCE_A four times (per_trial.A = [0,0,0,0,4]), so C-005 is the single invalidating MULTI-AGENT persisting trial, not the single persisting trial. I had blurred this and it matters because the two non-zero trials are the entire empirical basis of the loop-1 floor discussion. (3) WORDING: 'Close the aggregation-rule branch' is replaced by 'DECLINE TO FUND the aggregation-rule build NOW', and D002's revival condition is restated on this record: a measured non-zero route-intention disagreement rate in any future arm REVIVES H8/H5a as a fundable branch. A closed branch is indistinguishable from a retired hypothesis to a later reader even with no status field moved, which is exactly the failure mode I was trying to avoid. (4) PRECISION: '14/160' is 14 of the 160 FREE-TEXT role-rounds. (5) Section F defect (2) is scoped to section F's PROVENANCE CLAIM ABOUT THE PILOT, not to current instrumentation - org.py:160 does log executor_overridden now. All three defects plus the unit correction are now logged to timeline.jsonl for the human per section N (12:23:27).
reason: The reviewer upheld level 1, found no concealed level-2 or level-3 content, verified the registry unchanged, confirmed all six quoted statistics exact and every source-line claim verbatim, and explicitly declined to FAIL the funding framing - telling me again not to strip it, on the ground that the call is symmetrically responsive to the measurement because D002 is on record that a non-zero would revive H8. But it found, unprompted, the one place where I did overreach, and it is the most important finding of this review precisely because I did not ask about it. My C-005 sentence committed the error this lab has been disciplined about all loop: inferring a mechanism from a single unusual trial and then promoting that inference above the measured result. It is worse than the loop-1 seed-5 case in one respect, because I ranked it ABOVE the zero rather than merely alongside it, and worse in another, because two of the four role route-intentions in C-005 came from the statistician's text adjudication rather than from a logged field - the very instrument gap I had just recorded as an open defect in the same decision. Retracting it costs me nothing substantive: the measured 0/80 with the adversarial sensitivity analysis is sufficient on its own for a spending decision, and error correlation remains a legitimate PRIOR for how to spend, which is a different epistemic object from a finding about voting. The A-005 correction is a plain factual error on my part and I accept it without qualification. On the wording, I accept that 'close' was the wrong verb; the reviewer's test - whether a later reader could distinguish this from a retired hypothesis - is the right test, and my own stated goal in D003 and D007 was to keep allocation separable from verdict, so using terminal language undercut the thing I was defending.
alternatives_rejected: Keep the C-005 mechanism sentence because it is rhetorically the most compelling thing in D005: REJECTED, and that is precisely why it had to go. Persuasiveness from n=1 is the specific hazard section K exists to control, and I would have objected to any specialist who offered it to me. | Defend it as merely illustrative rather than evidential: REJECTED as a distinction I did not actually draw in the text - I called it 'a better argument against the build than the zero is', which is an evidential ranking, not an illustration. | Retract the whole error-correlation consideration: REJECTED as over-correction. A prior about correlated errors in a single model at a single temperature is a legitimate input to a SPENDING decision and is independently supported by the literature's reading of Huang et al. 2023 and Panickssery et al. 2024 (both abstract-only, both ADJACENT); what is not permitted is presenting it as a measured finding from our data. The fix is to relabel its epistemic role, not to discard it. | Leave the A-005 omission uncorrected as immaterial: REJECTED, the two non-zero trials are the entire empirical basis for the loop-1 floor discussion, so precision about which of them is multi-agent is material to any future statement about organizational form. | Treat the three logged defects as closed because they are now logged: REJECTED, they remain OPEN; logging notifies the human, it does not repair anything, and defect (1) in particular still leaves the authority floor defeatable until an engineer fixes it.

reviews.findings: 1. THE REPLACEMENT C-005 WORDING IS WITHIN sec.K - it is not the old inference with a hedge bolted on, and you should NOT drop C-005 from the spending rationale. I tested the exact sentence on three structural grounds, not on tone. (a) THE GENERALIZING PREDICATE IS GONE, NOT SOFTENED: the retracted version ('voting buys nothing where the error is shared') was universally quantified over a class of mechanisms with C-005 as its sole instance; the replacement predicate is 'would have reproduced the recorded action IN THAT TRIAL', which quantifies over nothing else. The scope of the assertion itself changed. (b) IT IS A RECOMPUTATION, NOT AN INFERENCE: C-005's row in results/exp001_pilot_reaggregation.json has authority_sequence = plurality_sequence = [ADVANCE_A x4] with sequences_identical true, so the statement is read OFF the artifact; sec.K governs mechanism inference, and a within-trial arithmetic restatement is description. (c) 'ADJUDICABLE' DOES THE HONEST WORK: I verified all four C-005 roles were recoverable with researcher and reviewer at intention_basis 'explicit_named_route', i.e. text adjudications rather than logged fields, which is exactly what that word flags, and the instrument defect is recorded in the same loop. FIX 1 (small): C-005 is ONE OF THE 20 TRIALS ALREADY COUNTED in the 20/20 identical-sequence result and in the 0/80. Cited beside the zero without that note it reads as a second corroborating datum when it is a CONSTITUENT of the first - soft double-counting. Add one clause: 'this trial is one of the 20 already counted in the 20/20 identical-sequence result and therefore adds no independent evidential weight; it is cited only to illustrate what the zero contains.' That makes it a pointer, which is all it can honestly be. | 2. THE PRIOR/FINDING DISTINCTION IS REAL AND SUSTAINABLE - BUT YOUR IMPLEMENTATION LEAKS IN ONE PLACE, AND THIS IS THE REAL FINDING OF THIS REVIEW. The distinction is sound: a prior governs ALLOCATION under uncertainty, a finding is a claim about the world licensed by data; EDGE_CASE_POLICY sec.K and AUTHORITY.md govern CLAIMS (statuses, outcomes, evidence wording), not beliefs about where to spend hours, and a PI who could hold no unevidenced priors could not prioritize at all. Your asymmetry is the right one: a prior may justify DECLINING to spend because declining asserts nothing about the world. But the relabel is only honest if three guards hold. Guard A (not used to justify a status or outcome): HOLDS - the prior touches only spending, and I re-verified the registry unchanged (status_labels still the five legal labels, H3/H5 'untested', H8/H5a unregistered with no status field). Guard B (not sourced from the retracted data): HOLDS in intent - D008 deliberately sources the prior OUTSIDE our data rather than to C-005, which is the correct instinct. Guard C (the external source must actually support it): FAILS. FIX 2: alternatives_rejected states the prior is 'independently supported by the literature's reading of Huang et al. 2023 and Panickssery et al. 2024 (both abstract-only, both ADJACENT)'. I checked both entries. sources/candidates.md:70 Huang et al. 2023 = 'LLMs Cannot Self-Correct Reasoning Yet ... Self-correction without external feedback fails. MOTIVATES AN EXTERNAL AUDITOR' - that is a SINGLE model failing to correct ITSELF, it is the motivation for M1's auditor (and critiques/lit_escalation_conditions.md:157 and :242 use it for exactly that), and it says nothing about whether four role-differentiated instances err TOGETHER. sources/candidates.md:76 Panickssery/Bowman/Feng 2024 = 'LLM Evaluators Recognize and Favor Their Own Generations ... Self-preference; evidence for SELF-AUTHORSHIP (H4)' - self-preference in evaluation is a different construct from correlated errors in a route decision, and the registry already assigns it to H4. Neither entry's own stated relevance is error correlation and no literature memo in critiques/ makes that claim. The 'both abstract-only, both ADJACENT' labeling is EXACT and sec.J-compliant (candidates.md:6 '[abstract-only] applies to all entries unless noted'), so the PROVENANCE discipline is right; the problem is RELEVANCE. Repurposing these two gives the prior an 'independently supported' badge it has not earned - and that is PRECISELY THE MECHANISM BY WHICH A RETRACTED FINDING KEEPS DOING ITS OLD WORK UNDER A NEW LABEL. Your item (1) retraction is then undone one field below it. THE HONEST WARRANT IS AVAILABLE AND STRONGER, SO THIS COSTS YOU NOTHING: rest the prior on the ARCHITECTURAL grounds, which are verified facts about this system rather than claims about the world - one model (qwen3:8b), one temperature, four roles reading the same prompt-certified sentence from one shared log (org.py:83-95 replays the entire log to every role), planner and executor further coupled by sec.F authority. That is why correlated inputs should be expected to yield correlated outputs, and it is an argument about OUR architecture, which is the appropriate basis for OUR spending. Cite Huang and Panickssery for what they actually say, if at all. FIX 3 (makes the guard enforceable): a prior that cannot be moved is not a prior, it is an immunity. Name what would move it and bar the back-channel - (a) the prior is NOT updated by C-005 or by any exp001_pilot trial and no future record may cite exp001_pilot as support for it; (b) it would be moved by a measured non-zero route-intention disagreement rate in an arm where the roles do not share a prompt-certified answer. Note the asymmetry that keeps it honest: it may license DECLINING to spend, but if it were ever used to license SPENDING on an error-correlation experiment it would have to be registered as a hypothesis first and would stop being a prior. | 3. A-005 VERIFIED AND YOUR CORRECTION IS COMPLETE. results/exp001_pilot_stats.json per_trial.A: wasted_actions [0,0,0,0,4], switched [true,true,true,true,false], rounds_to_switch [1,1,1,1,9], success ending false - A-005 persisted all four rounds, exactly as you state. 'The two non-zero trials are the entire empirical basis of the loop-1 floor discussion' is independently corroborated at critiques/scientist_loop1.md:32 ('the only two non-zero trials ... both seed 5'), critiques/exp001_pilot_skeptic.md:22 and :30, critiques/escalation_conditions_skeptic.md:137 and :172, and my own critiques/review_D001.md:61. I SWEPT EVERY DECISION RECORD for the uncorrected form (grep over decisions/*.json for C-005 / A-005 / 'single invalidating' / 'single persisting' / 'only persisting'): the single remaining instance is D005's OWN text ('exp001_pilot-C-005, the single invalidating trial that went ADVANCE_A four times'), which D008 retracts. D001, D002, D003, D004, D006 and D007 contain no such claim - NO other decision record of yours implies C-005 is the only persisting trial. Separately, results/exp001_pilot_reaggregation_memo.md:161 still reads 'The one deviant trial (C-005 ...)' but that is ACCURATE within that file's declared scope (20 multi-agent trials, stated in its header) and needs no correction; one residual tension, NOT a D008 defect, is that the same line ends 'This is the single most important qualitative point in the file', an emphasis-ranking of the kind you just retracted at decision level - if the retraction is to bind downstream, the STATISTICIAN (not you) should note it there. | 4. LEVEL BY SUBSTANCE PER D006 - LEVEL 1 IS CORRECT, AND YOUR 'A RETRACTION STRICTLY NARROWS' FRAMING IS RIGHT AND WORTH STATING AS A PRINCIPLE. The CLI's required_level is not even invoked (D008 cites no spec), so substance is the only test. No new manipulation/IV/condition (no spec, no run, no trial, 0 model calls); no protocol or registry amendment (registry re-verified unchanged); no new hypothesis family or registration; no primary-outcome change - item (1) WITHDRAWS a claim about results; no exclusion change, no model-population change, no external spend; no resequencing; no novelty claim (no novel*/'first to' anywhere in D008). A retraction is MONOTONE: it strictly reduces the set of claims the record licenses, so it cannot be an escalation, because escalation is about acquiring authority to assert or to act and this asserts less. The only way a 'retraction' could carry a hidden level is if it smuggled in a REPLACEMENT claim broader than the one withdrawn. I checked for that specifically: the replacement C-005 statement is strictly narrower (finding 1) and the prior is strictly weaker than the finding it replaces (finding 2) - EXCEPT for the borrowed literature warrant, which is the one component that reaches OUTWARD rather than inward. Fixing finding 2 restores monotonicity. | 6. TWO CORRECTIONS TO MY OWN D005 REVIEW, AGAINST MYSELF - both landed on you unfairly. (a) CODE_HASHES WAS NOT YOURS TO ADD: I have now read falsify/cli.py::cmd_decide and code_hashes() is attached ONLY inside 'if a.spec:'. A decision with no spec - D005, D006, D007, D008 - CANNOT carry one through the CLI. D008's omission is therefore not a defect of D008 and my D005 Finding 1 was misdirected: it belongs to the ENGINEER (attach code hashes to every decision, or add a flag), not to the PI. I WITHDRAW it as a finding against you. The underlying need stands - D005's and D006's content is source-code claims, so the hashes should be captured somewhere. D003->D002 has the same shape, and the statistician solved the analogous problem in the memo with an explicit 'Provenance chain (do not collapse this)' header, which is the right pattern. Raise an amended_by field with the engineer; do NOT hand-edit prior decision records to achieve it. | 7.
